clusters.name: Your grandfather Gordon's death, 1989–1994
clusters.reason: Around your grandfather Gordon's stroke in June 1991, within the following years: your own shifts in sleep and functioning as you moved through secondary school and into the conservatory, your wrist injury stopping your playing that autumn, conflict with your closest friend Rafe, and your low functioning into the community college. Your mother's shifts beside these, her remarriage to Desmond in October 1992, and your father and stepmother's earlier separation. Your grandmother Winifred's thyroid surgery within a year of your grandfather's death. Your cousin Bella's melanoma treatment in 1994 fell nearby. Your functioning climbed again once you found your drive at the exchange in Lisbon in early 1994, so the period reaches to that turn.

clusters.name: Your grandmother Winifred's death, 2001–2004
clusters.reason: Around your grandmother Winifred's bowel cancer diagnosis in 2001 or 2002, within the following months: your own shifts in functioning as you burned out from performing and failed your audition for the national orchestra in early 2002. Your distance from your parents that autumn, your move away from Thornbury, a new relationship with Marisol that winter, the quick separation that autumn, and your deep depression once you were back. Your distance from your parents held through that winter, though your friends Corbin and Silas drew near. Your grandmother spent her final months in your mother's home that autumn of 2003, and you visited her hung over on your way to the airport, anxious and distant, in early 2004. She died in February 2004. Your anxiety and functioning shifted as you returned to your therapist and began to recover; the period settles by early 2004 as you took the first steps toward nursing.

clusters.name: Your grandmother Lorna's death, 2008
clusters.reason: Around your grandmother Lorna's death in January 2008, within the following months: your move to Alder Creek to build with Silas that summer, where you were too drained for your mother's calls. She pressed to visit you there, your anxiety rose, and when she arrived you kept the door shut on her. Within weeks you left for nursing school at Marlow Sound and stopped speaking to your mother; the silence held for roughly a year. Your aunt Imogen had a stroke that January with months of rehabilitation ahead. Your partner Wren's first child was born in 2010. The period settles once you were far enough into your nursing training and the acute silence between you and your mother had held long enough to shift the balance.

clusters.name: Wren's family's closeness, 2017–2019
clusters.reason: Around your marriage to Wren in March 2017, within the following years: your contact with your mother eased off slightly. Your cousin Alice was diagnosed with multiple sclerosis in October 2017. Your sister Tara married James in 2018, and your aunt Imogen's memory slipped further; she lashed out when muddled toward her son Hal. In October 2019, Wren became swamped with a street party, a fundraising dinner, and her mother's retirement party at the lake house. Your anxiety and her anxiety and functioning all shifted through those weeks. You overfunctioned, laying out a strict plan for her while wishing she could manage without you. Her family—her father Hugo, her brother Leo, and she—talk all day; nothing happens to one that the others don't hear. The weekend had a plan and settled, the dinner went well, but at the lake you were awake from the small hours with no more sleep, could only pull back as the others rose, and felt you did not belong. Wren's anxiety stayed high after, and long quiet drives home followed. The period holds through October as the family occasion passed and the acute flare settled, though the pattern of your distance at her family gatherings remained.
